notes:
Second-reviewer angle: raw-string parsing loop + decoder internals, grounded in the actual installed library source. Versions confirmed from node_modules package.json: query-string 6.1.0, decode-uri-component 0.2.0. Callers confirmed: only AuthForm.tsx:41 and SignupForm.tsx:26, both passing a React-Router `location.search` string into React.useState at render (so a throw would crash the auth render, but see settled CVE ruling below). No bugs found. Detail:

1) queryString.extract (index.js:extract) = `indexOf('?')`; -1 => ''. Walked every edge case: extract('')='' ; extract('?')=slice(1)='' ; extract('?a=b')='a=b' ; extract('a=b')='' (NO '?' => empty) ; extract('https://x?a=b&c=d')='a=b&c=d' (slices after FIRST '?'; a '?' inside a value stays in the value). The subsequent `.split('&')` yields [''] for the empty cases and the `param.length===0` guard skips them, so keysInOccurrenceOrder=[] with no crash. The extract-vs-parse divergence on a '?'-less bare query (extract='' drops utmData keys while parse still parses them) is real but NOT reachable: browser location.search is always '' or '?'-prefixed — this is the SETTLED '?'-less-unreachable LOW, not re-flagged.

2) '+'-before-decode matches parse exactly. Sanitizer: `param.replace(/\+/g,' ').split('=')[0]` then `decodeUriComponent(rawKey)`. parse (index.js:parse): `param.replace(/\+/g,' ').split('=')` then `decode(key)=decodeComponent(key)` = the SAME decode-uri-component. Both replace '+' on the whole param before split and both take the first split element as key => identical key derivation. Verified consistency for keys containing '=', encoded keys (`utm%5Fsource` -> both decode to 'utm_source' and route to the utmSource top-level field, not utmData), and multi-'=' values.

3) decodeUriComponent malformed-input walk (decode-uri-component 0.2.0 index.js): rawKey is always a string so the `typeof !== 'string'` TypeError path is dead. Traced '%' and '%zz': built-in decodeURIComponent throws URIError -> catch -> customDecodeURIComponent, where multiMatcher `(%[a-f0-9]{2})+` finds no match, while-loop is skipped, and the input is returned unchanged (no throw). The genuine 0.2.0 crash payloads (the CVE-2022-38900 DoS) require attacker-crafted URLs and are the SETTLED 'decode-uri-component 0.2.0 CVE' LOW — not re-flagged; not reachable from a normal URL.

4) Dedup via `indexOf(decodedKey)===-1` records only the FIRST occurrence of each distinct key, matching sanitizeTrackingValue keeping value[0] (parse builds repeated-param arrays in occurrence order under arrayFormat:'none'). The 10-cap therefore counts DISTINCT keys — correct.

5) utm_ filter is a prefix test (`indexOf('utm_')===0`) that explicitly excludes 'utm_source'/'utm_campaign' and requires `parsedParams[key] !== undefined`; internal_ref (no 'utm_' prefix) correctly stays a top-level field and never enters utmData. Confirmed the filter runs BEFORE `.slice(0,10)`, so utm_source/utm_campaign never consume cap slots (spec: '10 utm_* keys beyond utm_source/utm_campaign'). For real '?'-prefixed input extract and parse split the identical '&'-content with identical key decoding, so every utm_ key in keysInOccurrenceOrder is present in parsedParams; the `parsedParams[key] !== undefined` guard is defensive-only (it would only bite in the unreachable '?'-less path) and, crucially, prevents `sanitizeTrackingValue(undefined)` from writing an undefined value — no fabrication. A valueless `?utm_x` parses to null, passes the `!== undefined` guard, and sanitizeTrackingValue returns null as-is (spec 5.1) — not a fabricated fallback.

6) utmData object built only inside `if (utmDataKeys.length > 0)`, so trackingParams.utmData is undefined (never {}) when no extra utm_* keys exist — matches spec 'utm_data must be nil/absent, never empty object'. No `|| ''`, `|| {}`, or `|| 0` anywhere (rule 13 clean).

7) Surrogate trim (sanitizeTrackingValue): only a trailing HIGH surrogate (0xD800-0xDBFF) is dropped. Verified this is correct — a slice at index 255 can only orphan a HIGH surrogate (its low pair falls at index 255+ and is cut); a trailing LOW surrogate at index 254 is always the valid second half of a pair kept intact, so leaving it is right. Dropping ANY trailing lone high surrogate (even sub-255) is strictly safe since a trailing lone high surrogate is never valid data and would emit an unpaired \udXXX that Rails json 2.6.1 400s. Empty-string path: `''.charCodeAt(-1)` = NaN, `NaN >= 0xD800` is false, returns '' — no crash. Non-string values (null, or null as array[0]) short-circuit via the `!isString` return. Surrogate-safe truncation is the qa-run-2 l2-B1 fix, not new.

8) No prototype-pollution surface: parsedParams is Object.create(null); utmData keys must start with 'utm_' so they can never equal '__proto__'/'constructor'; trackingParams/utmData are plain objects with own-property assignment only.

Conclusion: sanitizeTrackingParams + sanitizeTrackingValue are correct against the library internals for all realistic and crafted inputs I walked. No new (non-settled) findings.
